tracker.euros_help: Cash: real winnings in €. Tournaments: result of each tournament (prizes + bounties + tickets − buy-ins). Otherwise: in big blinds.
tracker.eur_cash_only: In €, only cash hands have a direct value; tournaments are counted per tournament (Tournaments tab).

graph.help_bb: "At showdown" = hands that reached showdown; "Without showdown" = pots won or lost before. A falling non-showdown line means you give up too many pots.
graph.title_tourney: Tournaments: cumulative result (€), tournament by tournament
graph.help_eur: Real result of each tournament: prizes + bounties + tickets − (buy-in + fee) × entries. Tournaments without a Winamax summary are not counted.

editor.name: Display name
editor.help: A stat is a ratio: "times / opportunities". Example: cnt_3bet / opp_3bet = your 3-bets divided by your 3-bet opportunities. Operations: + - * / ( ) and if(condition, then, else). Available counters:
editor.help_where: Condition: position = 'BTN', game_type = 'cash', stack_bb < 20, players = 3… combined with and / or / not.
editor.pick: Pick a stat on the left to edit it, or create your own.

tracker.export_csv_hands: Export up to 1,000 hands as CSV

review.title: Session review
review.tilt: Careful: you played many more hands than usual this session (VPIP +10 points or more). Possible tilt or fatigue.
review.disclaimer: These tips come from classic poker rules applied after the fact to finished hands: things to look at again, not a verdict. Solver analysis comes in phase 6.
review.nothing_to_review: Nothing special to review this session. Well played!

open_limp.title: Open limp
open_limp.why: Entering the pot first by just calling the big blind is rarely profitable: raise to take the initiative, or fold.

weak_shove.title: Shove with {{hand}} at {{stack}} bb
weak_shove.why: With more than 15 bb, shoving a weak hand risks a lot to win the blinds. At this depth a normal raise or a fold is usually better.

raise_fold_short.title: Raise-fold at {{stack}} bb
raise_fold_short.why: With 12 bb or less, raising without going all-in then folding cost you {{lost}} bb. At this depth it is usually shove or fold.

premium_fold.title: Folded {{hand}} preflop
premium_fold.why: {{hand}} is one of the 5 best starting hands. Folding it preflop against so little action is almost always a mistake (barring extreme ICM).

sb_flat.title: Small-blind call with {{hand}}
sb_flat.why: Calling a raise from the small blind means playing out of position with the big blind still behind. 3-bet or fold is usually better.

river_call_lost.title: Lost river call ({{lost}} bb)
river_call_lost.why: You called a big river bet (at least half the pot) and lost. Replay it: did your opponent usually have better on that line?

big_fold.title: Folded after investing {{lost}} bb
big_fold.why: You folded after putting in a big part of your stack. Either go all the way or stop earlier: find the street where you should have decided.

steal_won.title: Successful steal (+{{won}} bb)
steal_won.why: Folded to you, your raise took the blinds unopposed. These small pots add up.

three_bet_won.title: Winning 3-bet with {{hand}} (+{{won}} bb)
three_bet_won.why: Your preflop re-raise paid off: you took the initiative and won the hand.

cbet_won.title: C-bet takes the pot (+{{won}} bb)
cbet_won.why: After raising preflop, your flop bet made your opponent fold: good continuation.

value_bet.title: Value bet paid (+{{won}} bb)
value_bet.why: You bet or raised the river and got called by worse: you got the most out of your hand.

short_shove.title: Good shove at {{stack}} bb with {{hand}}
short_shove.why: With 10 bb or less, shoving first in with a solid hand is the right strategy.

big_pot.title: Big pot won (+{{won}} bb)
big_pot.why: One of the big hands of your session: replay it to see what worked.

leaks.intro: Your stats against winning-player targets, by format. "Leak" = certain even allowing for luck (95 % confidence interval). "Watch" = keep an eye on it. Edit targets in Settings → leaks/targets.toml.
leaks.not_enough: Not enough hands yet to find leaks (at least 20 opportunities per stat).
leaks.impact: Your result in this spot: {{done}} bb/100 when you do it, {{not}} bb/100 when you don't.

grid.help: Row and column = the two cards. Above the diagonal: suited (s); below: offsuit (o); diagonal: pairs. Hover a cell for details.

bankroll.none: No movement yet. Add your first deposit to track your bankroll.
bankroll.rule_ok: Your bankroll is {{n}} average buy-ins ({{avg}}). Above 30 you have room.
bankroll.rule_low: Careful: your bankroll is only {{n}} average buy-ins ({{avg}}). At least 30 buy-ins is advised for tournaments: move down or top up.

equity.need_board: Put 3 to 5 cards on the board to see what the range hits.
equity.keep_help: The range keeps only the ticked rows: then add the turn (and the river) for the next street.

icm.bad_prizes: Invalid prizes: write amounts separated by commas, e.g. 50, 30, 20.
icm.bubble_help: Row against column: what you lose by losing an all-in against that player, divided by what you win by winning it. 1 = chips are worth their weight in €. Hover a cell for the risk premium.

pf.model_help: Model: shove or fold, then the first caller goes to showdown. Blinds 0.5 / 1 bb. Preflop equities are exact, with card removal.
pf.lock_help: Enter the villain's real range (e.g. from his stats): the solver computes the other players' best response.

review.help: Review of shove/fold decisions at 20 bb or less. Without prizes: chip EV only. ICM only knows the players at the table; add the other tables' stacks if you know them.
review.bad: You chose "{{c}}"; the best option was "{{b}}".
review.chips_only: Without a payout structure, the review is in chip EV.

quiz.help: Random spots (chip EV, 2 to 6 players, 3 to 15 bb): choose shove or fold, scored by the equilibrium. Full drills come in phase 8.
quiz.detail: {{hand}}: EV of acting {{a}} bb, EV of folding {{f}} bb.

payouts.none: No structure yet. Enter one from a tournament lobby ("Prizes" tab).
payouts.help: Enter the prizes per place as shown in the Winamax lobby (they depend on the number of entrants). You can also paste a "place;prize" CSV.
payouts.csv_error: Unreadable CSV: one line per place, "place;prize" or amounts separated by commas.

tree.title: Bet tree
tree.add_allin: Add all-in if bet ≤ N pots
tree.help: Sizes: "33%" of the pot, "3x" the last bet, "e" geometric, "a" all-in, several separated by commas. Empty donk = same sizes as bets. Trees can also be edited in Settings > Solver trees.

solver.name: Solution name
solver.estimate: {{nodes}} decision nodes, {{oop}} OOP hands vs {{ip}} IP, about {{mb}} MB of memory.
solver.over_cap: Above the cap: enable compression, simplify the tree or raise the cap.
solver.with_locks: {{n}} locked node(s) will be applied to the next solve.

viewer.none: No solution loaded: start a solve or open one from the library.
viewer.not_in_range: Not in the range at this node.
viewer.lock_help: Fix each action's frequency for the whole range (e.g. "bet 100 %"), then re-solve: the rest of the tree adapts.
viewer.lock_added: Lock added: re-solve to apply it.

compare.b: Solution B (picked with "Compare" in the library)
compare.help: Open one solution with "Open" (A) and another with "Compare" (B), e.g. two bet trees on the same spot.

batch.help: The spot of the "New solve" tab (ranges, pot, stack, tree) is solved on each chosen flop, one after another. Every solution goes to the library. Allow time: run many flops overnight.
batch.uses: Ranges, pot, stack and tree come from "New solve" (the board {{board}} is replaced by each flop).

preflop.pick_chart: Pick a situation on the left, or create a chart folder for a format.
preflop.created: {{n}} situation(s) created in "{{folder}}", empty: fill them with the editor.
preflop.transfer_help: Format: a "[name]" line with the range below. PioSOLVER / GTO+ ranges ("AA:1.0, AKs:0.5") are accepted. No range ships with the app: everything comes from you or the solver.

solver.help: Simplified tree: open, 3-bet, 4-bet and all-in with fixed sizes. Heads-up it is exact; with more players, the first one to answer the open is the only opponent left (approximation). When the flop is seen without an all-in, each player realises the given share of their equity (1 = all of it). Playability above 1 makes strong hands realise more than their equity and weak hands less; rake is only taken when the flop is seen.
solver.to_act: {{who}} to act ({{p}} % of hands get here)
solver.end_showdown: End: all-in and showdown, pot {{pot}} bb.
solver.end_flop: End: the flop is seen, pot {{pot}} bb.
solver.grid_help: Each cell's height is how much of the hand is still played here; the colours are its action mix.

trainer.session: Session: {{n}} question(s), average loss {{avg}} bb, {{best}} good answer(s)

settings.title: Trainer: grade thresholds (loss in % of pot)

post.no_solution: No cached solution: solve a spot in the Solver module (or run a batch), then come back.
post.family: Every solution of the same spot (other boards)

pre.help: Questions come from your charts (Preflop module). The grade depends on how often the chart takes your action: the most frequent one is best.

ana.help: Analyse your hands against the solver: heads-up pots that see the flop. Ranges come from the chosen format's charts (open, call, 3-bet) and every postflop decision is compared with the solution.
ana.fairplay: The analysis runs in the background; it pauses as soon as a table is open and respects the memory cap of the settings. Each solved spot goes to the solver cache.
ana.leaks: Leaks by kind of spot (average loss per decision)

sheet.estimate: The strongest {{p}} % of hands, from the stats. An estimate: players do not play exactly the best hands.
